findings.title: Default CA loading can break requests import
findings.why_it_matters: The default CA bundle is now opened and parsed while importing adapters, which requests imports through its public sessions module. If the bundle is absent, unreadable, malformed, or cannot be extracted in a packaged install, the import raises before callers can use plain HTTP, verify=False, or a custom CA path. Previously this failure was deferred until a verified HTTPS request that needed the default bundle.
evidence: src/requests/__init__.py:160 imports .api and :174 imports .sessions; src/requests/sessions.py:15 imports HTTPAdapter from .adapters
src/requests/adapters.py:297-317 previously deferred default CA resolution and existence validation to cert_verify() for verified HTTPS requests
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize the default context lazily on the first verified HTTPS request, or otherwise defer/report default-bundle load errors at that request boundary so imports and requests using HTTP, verify=False, or a custom CA path remain usable.

testing_gaps: No tests were run, per assignment. The import-time failure behavior was established by source inspection; imports with a missing/unreadable default CA bundle, including packaged/zipapp extraction cases, were not exercised.
